hints: Focus on which carbon-halogen bond breaks most easily when warmed with aqueous silver nitrate.
Recall that the precipitate forms immediately, so the weakest C-X bond reacts first and remember the colour for its silver halide.
Think about which halogen in compound X is replaced by OH first while the two C-Cl groups stay unchanged for now.
walkthrough:
**Recall the silver nitrate test for halogenoalkanes**

Warm aqueous silver nitrate hydrolyses the C-X bond to release $X^-$. This then precipitates as $AgX$.

$$R-X + H_2O \rightarrow R-OH + H^+ + X^-$$
$$Ag^+(aq) + X^-(aq) \rightarrow AgX(s)$$

**Decide which halogen reacts first**

Bond strength decreases down the group: $C-Cl > C-Br > C-I$. So the $C-I$ bond is weakest and hydrolyses fastest.

Compound X has one $C-I$ and two $C-Cl$ bonds, so the $C-I$ bond reacts immediately.

**Identify the precipitate colour and first product**

$I^-$ gives $AgI$, which is yellow. Only the iodine is replaced by $OH$ in the first step, both chlorine atoms remain.

$$R-I \rightarrow R-OH \text{ with } CH_2Cl \text{ and ring } Cl \text{ unchanged}$$

**Match to the options**

Yellow precipitate plus replacement of only the ring $I$ by $OH$ matches the structure where $CH_2Cl$ and ring $Cl$ are still present.

options.A: Cream is the colour of $AgBr$, not present here. The organic product is also wrong because it shows the ring $C-Cl$ replaced by $OH$ while $CH_2Cl$ remains. The $C-Cl$ bond is stronger than $C-I$ and would not react first.
options.B: Cream suggests bromide, but X contains only Cl and I. The product showing all three halogens replaced by $OH$ is wrong because hydrolysis is stepwise. Only the fastest $C-I$ bond reacts immediately, not all three at once.
options.C: White is the colour of $AgCl$. $C-Cl$ hydrolysis is much slower than $C-I$ hydrolysis, so it would not give an immediate precipitate. The product is also reversed, it keeps the $I$ and replaces the $Cl$ atoms, which is opposite to bond strength order.
options.D: Yellow is correct for $AgI(s)$ from the fast hydrolysis of the $C-I$ bond. The organic product correctly shows only $I$ replaced by $OH$, with both $CH_2Cl$ and ring $Cl$ unchanged. This is the expected first hydrolysis product.
